pr_title: Role APIs allow internal role names
pr_body:
Internal users have internal role names associated with them (e.g.,
`_system` and `_xpack`). Currently, these role names are "reserved" in
that end-users can't create roles with clashing names. This PR removes
this restriction. The reasoning is similar to #86326:

For one, internal role names are not directly used during
authorization. Authorization for internal users follows a separate
path, leveraging the role descriptor that each internal user defines
directly. As such, internal roles and end-user defined roles do not
interfere with each other.

By removing the restriction, the PR decouples the implementation
details of internal users from our end-user APIs, which allows us to
evolve these details without introducing breaking changes.

Closes #86480
pr_comments: Hi @n1v0lg, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: Internal role names are (also) not special
issue_context.body:
### Description

Internal users have internal role names associated with them (e.g., `_system` and `_xpack`). Currently, these role names are "reserved" in that end-users can't create roles with clashing names. We should remove this restriction. The reasoning is similar to #86326:

For one, internal role names are not directly used during authorization. Authorization for internal users follows a separate path, leveraging the role descriptor that each internal user defines directly (e.g. see [SecurityProfileUser](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/security/user/SecurityProfileUser.java#L22-L36)). As such, internal roles and end-user defined roles do not interfere with each other.

By removing the restriction, we further decouple the implementation details of internal users from our end-user APIs, which allows us to evolve these details without introducing breaking changes.

To guard against the role name of an internal user resolving to an end-user defined-role erroneously, we should modify the internal user classes to only use the role name in the role descriptor, but exclude it from role names associated with the user instance.

review_comments: Similar to the above. But in this case, such a test already exists in `CompositeRolesStoreTests` as `testDoesNotUseRolesStoreForXPacAndAsyncSearchUser` and `testGetRolesForSystemUserThrowsException`.

This test has a positve assertion that the created user with given role can do something (read from index `idx`). Since we expand the tests to cover internal names, it is worthwhile to also add a negative assertion, e.g. the user is *not* able to perform an action that is not granted by the role. So we can be sure the role is correctly loaded, i.e. not accidentally load an internal role with the same name.
Absolutely, happy to add a negative test 👍

I've added a negative assertion (`assertClusterHealthOnlyAuthorizesWhenAnonymousRoleActive`) which was already conveniently used in other tests, along with a new integration test (`InternalUserAndRoleIntegTests`) 👍

I think this is not the right test for the changes. The change is to (1) allow user-defined roles to use internal names (CRUD operations) and also (2) a role name like `_system` should be resolved correctly to the user-define role, not the internal one. 

I believe the test here is more for (2). But the critical piece of "resolving role names to roleDescriptors" is mocked out with `roleMap` and `buildRole(...)`. So what it really exercises is the orchestration logic and also RBACEngine with given roleDescriptor. The better place to test "resolving role names to roleDescriptors" is `CompositeRolesStoreTests`

The system user (and its role) is special, in that there is additional logic in `AuthorizationService` that deals with it, before we even get to the role store:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/x-pack/plugin/security/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/security/authz/AuthorizationService.java#L255-L258

and

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/x-pack/plugin/security/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/security/authz/AuthorizationService.java#L615-L625

I intended this and the second test to cover that logic, and the tests I added (or extended) in `CompositeRolesStoreTests` to handle the other resolving role name scenarios.

I agree that this test is less focused on role resolution and more on internal users and would have been better placed in my previous PR. Since it does give us additional coverage of a path that is closely related to role resolution I think it still makes sense to keep. WDYT?

> I agree that this test is less focused on role resolution and more on internal users and would have been better placed in my previous PR. Since it does give us additional coverage of a path that is closely related to role resolution I think it still makes sense to keep. WYT?

OK. It's indeed more in context for #86398. I have no problem for you to keep it here. My main point is to make sure there is a test for CompositeRolesStore that checks:
(1) A role name like `_xpack_security` will _not_ be resolved to the internal role definition
(2) An internal user such as `XpackSecurityUser` can still get its role resolved correctly regardless whether there is an user-defined role called `_xpack_security`.

Some of those probably already exist. But it would be great if you could verify.

Makes sense! I've added added explicit tests for (1). 

For (2), `testDoesNotUseRolesStoreInternalUsers` verifies that there were no interactions with the stores, and `testGetRoleDescriptorsListForInternalUsers` does not even mock them; this should implicitly cover the assertion that resolution works regardless whether there is an user-defined role with a matching name.
